Hi Rachel — thanks for the clear ask. Below is a concise mapping; I've attached a one‑pager and three small artifacts. Happy to jump on a 30‑min walkthrough if you'd like.

Quick mapping (summary):

- Hosted (Redwood API - multi-tenant hosted):
  • Data residency: customer data is stored on shared infrastructure logically isolated by tenant. No customer-dedicated hardware by default.
  • Key management: Redwood manages disk encryption keys by default; customers on enterprise plans can bring keys via KMS integration (customer KMS in Dedicated/Private or BYOK for some Hosted tiers).
  • Network isolation: TLS in transit; VPC peering/PrivateLink for enterprise Hosted customers; full tenant isolation available on Dedicated/Private.
  • SIG scope guidance: Controls that require customer-managed physical isolation are "out of scope" for Hosted; logical controls and encryption-in-flight/at-rest are Redwood-managed.

- Dedicated (reserved capacity / tenant-isolated pools):
  • Data residency: workload runs on reserved GPU pools; hardware not shared with unrelated tenants in the customer's capacity region.
  • Key management: supports customer KMS via dedicated configuration; Redwood can assist with key rotation policies.
  • Network isolation: dedicated subnets, optional private endpoints, and stricter routing policies; suitable where hardware-level separation is required.
  • SIG scope guidance: Many infrastructure and operational controls remain Redwood-managed; physical isolation and hardware tenancy items may be considered customer-provided if specifically contracted.

- Private (VPC / on‑prem):
  • Data residency: deployed into customer VPC or on-premises cluster; customer controls hardware and physical access.
  • Key management: customer-managed KMS/HSM (Redwood integrates but does not hold keys by default).
  • Network isolation: full customer network control; Redwood's control plane can be configured to minimize egress depending on deployment.
  • SIG scope guidance: Customer owns most infrastructure-level controls; Redwood retains responsibility for application and runtime patches if management agreement includes it.

Attachments included:
- redwood_runtime_modes_SIG_onepager.pdf (one‑page mapping)
- redwood_kms_key_management_snippet.txt (suggested SIG language for key ownership)
- network_topology_diagram.png (high-level Hosted/Dedicated/Private diagram)

For your specific asks:
- One-line suggested SIG answer for "Is customer data stored on shared hardware?":
  • Hosted: "Yes — customer data is stored on logically isolated storage on shared infrastructure managed by Redwood."
  • Dedicated: "No — workloads run on reserved capacity pools that are not shared with unrelated tenants by default."
  • Private/VPC/on‑prem: "No — deployed into customer-controlled hardware or VPC, under the customer's physical control."

- Audit log exports: Hosted: we offer scheduled exports (monthly) to customer S3 buckets or Secure Drive for enterprise customers; Dedicated/Private: exports are configurable and can be pushed to customer log endpoints.

Let me know if you want the one‑line phrasing adjusted for SIG tone; I'm copying Jordan and Aditya for any technical clarifications on routing and evidence.

Best,
